typical-leaf-curl-en.raw:
{
  "observedSigns": [
    "Tomato leaves curling upward",
    "Leaves feel stiff to the touch",
    "Plants still maintain a green color"
  ],
  "possibleCauses": [
    "Environmental stress such as high heat or moisture fluctuation",
    "Viral infections like Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus",
    "Herbicide drift or chemical exposure"
  ],
  "followUpQuestions": [
    "Are all the tomato plants affected or only a few?",
    "Have you noticed any whiteflies or other tiny insects on the underside of the leaves?",
    "How regular is your watering schedule recently?"
  ],
  "immediateActions": [
    "Ensure consistent watering without waterlogging the soil",
    "Monitor the plants closely for any spreading of the curl or color changes",
    "Take clear photos of the affected leaves for future reference"

typical-wilting-en.raw:
{
  "observedSigns": [
    "Tomato plants wilting during the middle of the day",
    "Soil is described as moist",
    "Some plants have died within a week"
  ],
  "possibleCauses": [
    "Bacterial wilt",
    "Root rot due to excessive moisture",
    "Stem borer damage restricting water transport"
  ],
  "followUpQuestions": [
    "Do you notice any brown discoloration inside the stem if you cut it open?",
    "Is there a white ooze coming out when you cut a stem and place it in clear water?",
    "Are these symptoms affecting scattered plants or whole rows?"
  ],
  "immediateActions": [
    "Remove and safely destroy severely wilted or dead plants to prevent the spread of disease",
    "Avoid moving soil or water from affected areas to healthy parts of the farm",
    "Ensure proper drainage if water is pooling around the roots"
  ],
  "whenToSeekHelp": "Consult a local agricultural extension worker immediately, especially since plants are dying quickly and the cause could be a fast-spreading soil-borne disease like bacterial wilt.",
  "uncertainty": {
    "level": "high",
    "reason": "Rapid wilting with moist soil can be caused by several different vascular diseases or root issues that cannot be confirmed without field inspection and plant tissue testing."
  }
}
